description: A Number Series is a sequence of numbers that follows a specific mathematical rule or pattern. In competitive exams, identifying this pattern is crucial to finding the missing or wrong number in the sequence.

sections.title: Basic Number Series
sections.description: The most common types of series based on a constant difference or a constant ratio between consecutive numbers.

key_concepts.explanation: A sequence where the difference between any two consecutive numbers remains constant.
A sequence where each subsequent number is obtained by multiplying the previous number by a fixed constant (ratio).

sections.title: Mixed and Exponential Patterns
sections.description: Sequences where squares, cubes, or combinations of two or more mathematical operations are used simultaneously.

sections.title: Systematic Approach to Solve
sections.description: A step-by-step process to quickly decode any unknown pattern in a number series.

steps.title: Find the Difference
steps.detail: Calculate the difference between consecutive numbers. If the difference increases gradually, it is likely an addition series.

steps.title: Check Double Difference
steps.detail: If no pattern is found in the first difference, calculate the difference of the differences (second-tier difference).

steps.title: Check the Growth Rate
steps.detail: If the numbers increase very rapidly, check for multiplication, square, or cube series patterns.

sections.title: Common Question Types
sections.description: The major formats of series questions frequently asked in competitive examinations.

results: Identify the pattern from the available sequence of numbers.
Apply the rule to at least 3 consecutive numbers to confirm the pattern.
Apply the confirmed rule to the relevant position to find the final answer.
Discover the general rule that applies to the majority of the numbers in the series.
Locate the specific number that breaks this established rule.
Replace the wrong number with the correct one to ensure the entire series follows the overall pattern.
